title: Impact of Financial Literacy on Financial Performance in Select Multi-Purpose Cooperatives in Tagbilaran City, Bohol, Philippines
authors: Gudelosao, E.T.; Cafe, A.J.; Liray, K.; Tabaco, J.G.; Felicitas, L.N.
tldr: Financial attitude fully mediates the relationship between financial knowledge and behavior, but member financial literacy alone does not predict cooperative performance.
problem_and_motivation: Cooperatives play a vital role in economic growth and financial inclusion, especially in communities with limited formal financial access. Many cooperative members exhibit low financial literacy affecting their decisions and organizational performance. The direct link between member financial literacy and institutional performance remains under-researched in local contexts.
approach: Employed quantitative descriptive-correlational research design with mediation analysis.
Surveyed 100 members from four registered multi-purpose cooperatives in Tagbilaran City.
Used structured questionnaire adapted from OECD/INFE guidelines with 30 items across three constructs.
Analyzed cooperative financial statements using CDA STEPS method for performance evaluation.
Applied PROCESS Model for mediation analysis and simple linear regression for performance prediction.
findings: num: Financial knowledge significantly increases financial attitude (β = 0.525, p < .001).
num: Financial attitude significantly increases financial behavior (β = 0.592, p < .001).
num: Financial knowledge has no significant direct effect on behavior (β = 0.024, p = .797).
num: Financial attitude fully mediates knowledge-behavior pathway (indirect effect β = 0.311, p < .001).
num: Financial literacy explains only 0.2% of variance in cooperative performance (R² = 0.002).
key_figures_tables: Table 2: Financial literacy levels → Members show High literacy across knowledge, attitude, and behavior.
Table 3: Direct effects → Attitude mediates knowledge-behavior relationship.
Table 4: Indirect effects → Full mediation confirmed through bootstrapping.
Table 5: Cooperative performance → Most cooperatives fall within Fair performance range.
Table 6: Regression analysis → Financial literacy does not significantly predict performance.

key_equations.explanation: Indirect effect of financial knowledge on behavior through attitude mediation.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This study quantifies the mediating role of financial attitude in translating knowledge to behavior among cooperative members. It demonstrates that knowledge alone does not directly influence behavior without attitudinal change. The research shows member financial literacy has minimal predictive power on organizational performance. Findings suggest governance and management factors are more influential than individual member literacy.
directly_justifies: Financial attitude fully mediates the relationship between knowledge and behavior.
Financial literacy explains only 0.2% of variance in cooperative performance.
Organizational factors likely exert more substantial impact on performance than member literacy.
Attitude-focused training may be more effective than knowledge-heavy approaches.
limits: Limited to four cooperatives in Tagbilaran City, Bohol.
Cross-sectional design does not establish causation.
Self-reported financial behavior may suffer from social desirability bias.
Does not account for cooperative-specific governance and management factors.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan of all topic domains identified high relevance for financial behavior (1.C) and financial behavioral profiles (5.A) due to core focus on literacy components. Medium relevance for budgeting strategies (7.A), evaluation frameworks (12.A), landscape of existing systems (4.A), culturally specific practices (2.A), and engagement dynamics (11.A) as supporting aspects. Low relevance for Filipino young professionals (1.A) and savings management (13.A) as contextual mentions. Domains related to predictive modeling, anomaly detection, and ML model serving were considered and rejected as not covered by this cooperative financial literacy study.
